message.content: Render the skeleton at the panel's real size and tell me if it is legible.

content.text:
## Legibility

The panel is 300 ppi, so a pixel size is not a text size. The first
renderer used a 26 pixel font, which works out at:

- 6.2 pt body text
- an x-height of 1.18 mm
- 48 lines on a 142 mm screen

That is roughly half the smallest size anyone sets a paperback in.

```python
def points_to_pixels(points, ppi):
    # a point is 1/72 inch, so a size needs a ppi to mean anything
    return round(points / 72 * ppi)
```

Body text is now 11 pt: 23 lines and about 51 characters a screen, with
an x-height of 2.03 mm. Both frame gates caught the change and the
references were regenerated.

The **panel** is 1264x1680 at 300 ppi, so a point size only means something through `Panel.ppi`. See [the rendering notes](https://example.com/rendering.md).

| finding | fix |
| --- | --- |
| body text at 6.2 pt | sizes go through the panel's density |
| true size nine per cent small | exact fractional scaling |

Wider tables stack instead:

| gate | catches | shown by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frames | a frame differing anywhere | moving the margin one pixel |
| views | a view laying out differently | merging the speaker labels |

Underscores in `klide_viewer.py` and *quiet* emphasis are left alone.
